answer: Divergent-Commitment Ledger: each identity must publish a signed, unique work product per horizon and relinquish its private key. A clone can copy public behavior but cannot produce divergent private signatures without splitting its key, which is detectable. Attackers pay one irrevocable key plus one workflow artifact per identity, and reuse across identities (like a glacier calving identical blocks) fails cross-checks. Each forged identity costs a distinct irreplaceable opal—something unique and non-clonable—plus the labor of maintaining separate histories.
